My example, I got a paper cut on my wrist and had to spend 3 days in hospital.

This was back in the days of chalkboards, I had a paper cut on my wrist, I prepared for a day of teaching, including wiping the chalkboard. Never thought a thing about it but perhaps some chalk dust got into the cut. I looked at my sore wrist at lunchtime (it was itching a bit and felt sore) and saw red lines running up my arm from the paper cut. They were only a few inches long so I thoroughly washed my wrist and left it at that.

End of the day I checked again, the red lines were up past my elbow and I vaguely remembered my Gran saying 'Red lines' were serious, so I went to hospital (UK here so cost/insurance was not an issue)

Walked into Accident and Emergency and they put me top of the list and put me on intravenous antibiotics for three days. Seems I had Lymphangitis ( commonly called Blood Poisoning)

The look on the HR managers face when I had to put 'paper cut' under cause of illness on my sick note will stay with me forever.

TL;DR Paper cut put me in hospital for 3 days
What is the Most Ridiculous reason for you having to take time off work?

I once accepted to permanently work a shift I knew I could never cover. My friend had just moved to the city and I did not want him to be working the second shift every Friday night (5pm-1am). I had been working at the company for a few years at that point so each week I just bullied a more junior employee into covering that shift or made up an excuse. I once forgot to get a cover so I left a note where I should have been saying, "Whoops, forgot to get a cover." I did not put down the hours, and the fact that no one was there as well as the note never got brought up. After about half a year of this going on my boss asked me what was happening and I told him what was going on. He laughed and gave that shift to a junior employee that was not my friend.

Being hospitalized is not a ridiculous reason to call off of work. At least not by my standards.

I had a few jobs in college that required me to work all sorts of crazy hours. It's hard to even describe just how insane my work schedule could be, because most people were also in college, and could not work consistent hours and consistent days. I have worked on literally every holiday in existence -- you name it, I've worked it. This first example technically doesn't qualify, but for one job I had, my status was pretty high, and I had priority for creating my hours. And in addition to structuring work hours around my courses, I would also structure them around the broadcast of Survivor on Thursday evenings.

But, if we are talking about having actually taken off of work for something, then I would say that "calling in" for the sake of watching the Academy Awards is probably at the top of the list, which I've done three or four times. Interestingly, it's never been a big deal. Since the Oscars are usually within a few weeks of Valentine's Day, it has always been incredibly easy to exchange favors with co-workers. Everyone always wants to take Valentine's Day off, and I'm always willing to cover it for someone. People always felt like they were getting the better end of the deal by agreeing to work on a Sunday night in late February if it meant they could spend Valentine's Day with their significant other. Fine by me. I celebrate Valentine's Day sometime between February 15th and the 19th, anyway. I don't know how people can stand to wait four hours for a table at a restaurant, and then wait two more hours for their food to arrive. It amazes me that society decided as a collective to have the exact same date night, once a year, resulting in the least optimal conditions imaginable for romance.
